name: icmSendAtt
label: Send Attitude (127257)
description: send NMEA2000 Attitude (roll/pitch) from the ICM-20948 IMU. Turn off while calibrating if you don't want uncalibrated values on the bus.

name: icmUseDmp
label: Use sensor fusion (DMP)
description: use the chip's onboard sensor fusion (accel+gyro+compass fused in hardware) instead of the plain accelerometer tilt calculation and separate compass math. More accurate and far more stable once there's real boat motion - a plain accelerometer can't tell gravity apart from the boat's own acceleration, gyro fusion can. Falls back to the plain calculation automatically if fusion fails to initialize. Takes effect after Save (restarts and re-initializes the sensor). While this is on, the compass hard-iron offsets below do NOT apply - fusion calibrates the compass internally and we can't inject our own offset into that.

name: icmRollInv
label: Invert roll
description: flip the sign of roll before applying the offset below. NMEA2000 defines positive roll as tilted right (heeling to starboard) - heel the boat to a known side (or just prop it up) and check the "Roll (heel), calibrated" value on the IMU tab: if it reads NEGATIVE while heeling to starboard, enable this. Use this for a 180° mounting flip (about the roll or yaw axis), not the fine offset below - a sign flip and an additive offset are different corrections, one can't substitute for the other.

name: icmPitchInv
label: Invert pitch
description: flip the sign of pitch before applying the offset below. NMEA2000 defines positive pitch as the bow rising - lift the bow and check the "Pitch (trim), calibrated" value: if it reads NEGATIVE while the bow rises, enable this. Same 180°-mount case as the roll invert.

name: icmRollOff
label: Roll calibration offset
description: degrees added to the (possibly inverted) roll reading for fine calibration only - a few degrees, not for correcting a 180° mounting error, use Invert roll for that. With the boat confirmed level, press the "C" button - it live-previews the negative of the current reading; type that number into the box and press Set.

name: icmPitchOff
label: Pitch calibration offset
description: degrees added to the (possibly inverted) pitch reading for fine calibration only - same procedure and same caveat as the roll offset.

name: icmSendHdg
label: Send Magnetic Heading (127250)
description: send NMEA2000 Magnetic Heading from the ICM-20948's compass. Defaults OFF on purpose - calibrate the fields below first (an uncalibrated heading on the bus is worse than none, since an autopilot or plotter could trust it). This is a simple hard-iron-only calibration, not a full compass swing with a deviation table - expect a few degrees of residual, heading-dependent error.

name: icmMagXOff
label: Compass X hard-iron offset
description: hard-iron offset for the magnetometer X axis - only used when "Use sensor fusion (DMP)" above is OFF (fusion calibrates the compass internally instead). Procedure: press Reset on the Status page for a clean start, then rotate the WHOLE BOAT slowly through at least one full circle (this is a compass swing - the sensor is bolted down, it can't be waved around like a handheld device) while watching the "C" button's live preview stabilize; then Set. Do this and the Y offset below together, same swing.

name: icmMagYOff
label: Compass Y hard-iron offset
description: hard-iron offset for the magnetometer Y axis - same compass-swing procedure as the X offset above, at the same time. Also only used when sensor fusion is OFF.

name: icmHdgInv
label: Invert heading
description: flip the sign of the computed heading before applying the offset below. Point the bow at a known heading (chart feature, sun position, another compass): if turning the bow to starboard makes the displayed heading DECREASE instead of increase, enable this - a mirrored axis needs a sign flip, not an offset, same reasoning as the roll/pitch inverts.

name: icmHdgOff
label: Heading calibration offset
description: degrees added to the (hard-iron corrected, possibly inverted) heading for fine calibration - do this AFTER the hard-iron offsets above. Point the bow at a precisely known heading, press the "C" button, type that known heading into the box - the preview automatically computes the correct offset from the live reading - then Set.

name: icmSendRot
label: Send Rate of Turn (127251)
description: send NMEA2000 Rate of Turn from the gyroscope's Z axis - a direct hardware measurement, not derived from the (slower, smoothed) heading value, so it responds immediately to an actual turn. Unlike heading, this doesn't need a compass swing to be trustworthy - defaults on.

name: icmRotFiltAlpha
label: Rate of turn smoothing (1=none)
description: low-pass filter factor for Rate of Turn - 1.0 (default) applies no smoothing at all, exactly matching the original unfiltered gyro-Z reading. Lower values smooth more (0.1 is fairly heavy smoothing) at the cost of slower response to an actual turn. Provisional - real sensor noise characteristics aren't known without hardware.

name: icmRotInv
label: Invert rate of turn
description: flip the sign of rate of turn. NMEA2000 defines positive as turning to starboard - turn the bow to starboard and check the IMU tab: if the value reads NEGATIVE, enable this. Same reasoning as the roll/pitch/heading inverts - the chip's axis handedness isn't knowable from code.

name: icmAccRange
label: Accelerometer range
description: accelerometer full-scale range - narrower gives finer resolution but clips sooner. Boat motion is normally gentle enough that +/-2g is right; widen only if mounted somewhere that could see shock loads (e.g. slamming into waves) hard enough to clip a narrower range. Takes effect after Save (restarts and re-initializes the sensor).

name: icmGyrRange
label: Gyroscope range
description: gyroscope full-scale range - same tradeoff as the accelerometer range above. Boat rotation rates are normally gentle; widen only if something rotates unusually fast. Used directly by sensor fusion (DMP) when that's on; with fusion off this task doesn't read the gyro at all.

name: icmRateHz
label: Update rate (Hz)
description: how often to sample the sensor and send N2K Attitude/Heading, in Hz. The sensor itself already runs fast enough for this (magnetometer is configured for continuous 100Hz, accel/gyro run in continuous mode) - this is purely our own polling rate. Higher isn't free: more CAN bus traffic and I2C/CPU load, though at these rates that's still trivial for the ESP32-S3.

name: icmOrientation
label: Mounting orientation
description: which way the sensor is physically mounted relative to the boat. Forward (the default) reproduces the original wiring assumption exactly - changing this doesn't affect a currently-working installation unless you deliberately select a different value. The four flat options (Forward/Starboard/Aft/Port) are confirmed correct by construction; the 20 tilted/upside-down options are mathematically valid rotations but their exact real-world meaning is NOT yet confirmed against physical hardware - pick one, check the raw accelerometer/roll/pitch values on this tab against a known physical test (tilt the boat a known way), and correct if it doesn't match. See doc/IcmPhysicalTestProcedure.md.

name: icmHeadingMode
label: Heading source

list.l: Auto (prefers fusion, falls back to DMP, then compass)

description: which heading source drives PGN 127250 (subject to "Send Magnetic Heading" below still being on). Defaults to "DMP" specifically to match this task's original behavior (DMP yaw when sensor fusion is on) - unlike before, the DMP reading is now validated (staleness, quaternion sanity, disagreement with the independently-computed software compass) rather than trusted unconditionally, so a bad DMP sample now reports "no heading" instead of a wrong one. "Auto" is a deliberate opt-in, not the default, since it prefers the new software fusion source the moment it's valid - a currently-tuned installation's output shouldn't change just from this firmware update landing.

name: icmSrcTransMs
label: Heading source transition (ms)
description: when the active heading source changes (e.g. Auto mode switching from compass to fusion once fusion converges), blend circularly over this many milliseconds instead of jumping instantly. 0 disables blending (instant switch). Provisional default.

name: icmHdgFiltEn
label: Enable heading smoothing filter
description: smooths sample-to-sample heading noise from whichever source is active. Defaults OFF to exactly match the original code's behavior (no filtering happened before). A large jump (fast turn, or a source switch already handled by the transition blend above) always passes through unfiltered rather than being smoothed away.

name: icmHdgFiltTau
label: Heading filter time constant (s)
description: how quickly the smoothing filter above tracks a genuine (small) heading change - responds faster automatically while the boat is actively turning. Only used when the filter is enabled. Provisional default.

name: icmDevEnable
label: Enable compass deviation table
description: apply a boat-specific compass deviation table (built from a real compass swing against a trusted reference) on top of the hard-iron/soft-iron calibration and mounting offset above. Defaults OFF - no table exists until one is built via the web UI's deviation editor.
